label: Red Spring 1919
atlas_title: Atlas of Anti-Black Violence, Red Spring 1919
atlas_dek: Red Spring: the episodes of anti-Black violence reported in the Black press from March 1 to July 15, 1919, before the Red Summer, from our dossiers, placed on 1910 county lines and by month. Built from Black weeklies only; the white press is not searched. Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for episodes of anti-Black violence in the Black press from March 1 to July 15, 1919, the spring before the Red Summer. This collection is a test of our method on one kind of source: every dossier is built only from Black weeklies, with no white daily press. It stops on July 15, before the Washington and Norfolk riots, so later reports of spring events are not here.

The dossiers come from the 149 located events in our table for those issues. We did not write dossiers for 33 events: ten editorial lists of Georgia towns with no act described, two lynchings of white men (Jay Lynch at Lamar, Missouri, and Frank Foukal at Bay Minette, Alabama), and 21 earlier cases the papers retold, such as the Mary Turner lynching of 1918 and the East St. Louis riot of 1917. Three new events came from leads in the first dossiers and have their own entries.

Fifteen dossiers are set aside: a white man's beating at St. Joseph, Missouri; the Yale student and soldier riot; the legal hanging of John Snowden at Annapolis; five labor disputes and handbills with no force; and seven police killings and beatings where no report gives the victim’s race.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched the Black press only. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. Clippings are shown as page images.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
